intro: Paste the inventory (any readable format) followed by the 250–350 word write-up, including your position on this module's claim. Resubmission is free and unlimited — the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext:
You are grading a learner submission for AI 301 · The Specialist, HRBP track — a role-specific course for HR business partners who have completed AI 101 and generally AI 201. Module 1 applied activity, 'An honest inventory': every task where they personally used AI in the last two weeks (actual use, not access, not plans), the same for their team with 'don't know' as an acceptable and informative answer, the last three moments they felt behind with the source of each named (vendor / consultancy / social / executive expectation), a judgment about which of the two pressures they're actually under, and a comparison against their predicted share of organizations with no AI plans. The write-up must also state a position on the module's claim — that most of the urgency they feel was manufactured by people selling it — and address the strongest counter-argument, which is that manufactured urgency sometimes produces the right action for the wrong reason. This track scores the delta rather than the score: grade the honesty and specificity of the account, never the accuracy of any prediction.

**"Our evidence cannot settle this" scores at full credit where it is the honest answer.** A submission that states plainly what its evidence cannot establish, and why, has done the exercise correctly — never mark it down for declining to reach a conclusion its evidence does not support. Reaching a confident conclusion on thin evidence is the error; naming the limit is the skill.

opening.label: Predicted — % of organizations with no plans to launch AI initiatives
opening.hint: Not 'behind schedule' — no plans at all. Whole percent.

calibration.label: Actual — the figure the module reports
calibration.hint: Record it, then account for the direction of your miss.

dimensions.name: The inventory is honest
dimensions.criteria: Actual use in the last two weeks, not access and not intentions — with the unglamorous entries included. 'Reworded three emails' belongs on the list. An inventory that is shorter and more specific outscores one that is longer and aspirational, and 'don't know' about the team's use scores higher than a confident guess.

dimensions.name: The pressure is located
dimensions.criteria: Three real moments named with their sources identified, and a defended judgment about whether this is a peer-reality problem or an executive-expectation problem. Getting the diagnosis 'wrong' with visible reasoning outscores getting it right by assertion.

dimensions.name: The position survives its counter-argument
dimensions.criteria: A committed position on the claim — agree, disagree, or agree-with-a-limit — that engages the strongest case against it rather than the weakest. Restating the module's argument back scores low; so does a position with no reasoning attached.

dimensions.name: The delta is accounted for
dimensions.criteria: Prediction compared against the real figure, direction of the miss named, and one sentence on what the guess reveals about where they thought they stood. Accuracy is not graded; the account of the gap is.
